item.title: Inside Fraternity Movement, the student wing of Welfare Party of Umar Khalid’s father that joined so called anti-pollution protests
item.description: Just as it is the case with most leftist outfits, Fraternity Movement also packages itself as a defender of democratic principles, secularism, the constitution, social justice and whatnot; however, beyond the shiny packaging lies the dark and disturbing pro-Islamist and divisive activism. | OpIndia News

item.title: AWBI issues SOP on removal of stray dogs from insitutions on Supreme Court's directions
item.description: The AWBI SOP on removal of stray dogs orders States to identify every institution, prevent dog ingress, ensure daily waste control and shift all dogs found inside campuses to shelters, marking a decisive shift towards citizen and child safety. | OpIndia News

item.title: Reserve Bank replaces over 9,000 circulars with 244 master guidelines for 11 sectors
item.description: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday announced the issuance of 244 Consolidated Master Directions, scrapping 9,345 outdated and redundant circulars that had accumulated over seven decades.

item.description: Globally, Bangladesh is now among the worst performers in banking health, surpassed only by a few troubled economies such as Equatorial Guinea, San Marino, Ukraine, and Chad. | OpIndia News

item.title: PM Modi unveils 77-ft bronze statue of Lord Rama at Partagali Math in Goa: Read how it protected Hindus for centuries
item.description: The Partagali Math embodies the civilizational resilience that PM Modi often highlights. For centuries it protected Hindu faith in Goa during adversity, kept traditions alive through colonial suppression, and provided refuge, unity, and leadership. | OpIndia News

item.title: After causing devastation Sri Lanka Cyclone Ditwah reaches Indian coastal areas, IMD issues red alert
item.description: The cyclone caused massive devastation in Sri Lanka is tragic. More than 120 lives were lost and thousands were displaced. | OpIndia News

item.title: Explained: India finds new export markets to nullify the effects of steep US tariffs
item.description: Several Indian sectors that earlier depended heavily on the American market are now quickly redirecting their products to other regions. Items like shrimps, gems and jewellery, auto components, and electrical machinery have found many buyers in Asian and European countries. | OpIndia News
